security.title: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
security.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync derives fileCount from the client-controlled multipart Request.Files collection and loops from zero to fileCount without an application-level count limit. A request containing a very large number of files can force repeated per-file processing and blob upload operations.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.blobContainer is a mutable static field. Each concurrent Index request assigns a BlobContainerClient to it, while upload and delete requests read the same field without synchronization. Concurrent requests can overwrite or observe shared state without a defined ordering.

security.title: Missing Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: The static BlobContainerClient field is shared by concurrent ASP.NET requests. It is reassigned in Index and accessed in upload/delete actions without synchronization, so concurrent operations can race on the shared reference.

security.title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
security.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.Index creates the image container using PublicAccessType.Blob, making each blob publicly readable without an authenticated application check. This assigns public read permissions to uploaded gallery content.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The upload and deletion actions perform security-relevant storage changes but do not write audit or application logs for successful operations. Exceptions are placed in ViewData and returned to the caller instead of being recorded, leaving no server-side event trail for these changes or failures.

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes the client-supplied files[i].FileName directly to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string), which treats the string as a local file path. The path is not restricted to an upload directory, so crafted relative traversal components can cause the server to read a file outside the intended upload location.

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes the client-supplied files[i].FileName to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string) as a local file path without restricting or canonicalizing it. A crafted relative path containing traversal components can therefore select a file outside an intended upload directory.

security.title: Absolute Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync uses the client-supplied files[i].FileName as the local path passed to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string). No restriction prevents an absolute path from resolving to a server-side file outside an intended upload directory.

security.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
security.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync accepts all posted files without checking extension, content type, or file content before uploading them to the gallery container. The container is created with public blob access in HomeController.Index, and uploaded objects are exposed as browser-accessible blob URLs, allowing active content such as HTML or script-bearing image formats to be hosted without type restrictions.

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
security.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

evidence.explanation: DisplayFilesToUpload appends the user-controlled File.name value directly into an HTML string and assigns the string to FilesToUpload.innerHTML without HTML encoding. A filename containing markup can be interpreted as HTML or script by the browser.
